title: Rate Lock Commitment Relock Policy
content:
**Applies to:** an expired **Rate Lock Commitment**.

**(a) Relock window.** A relock at worst-case pricing is available only within the relock window that started on the lock expiration date. Count calendar days forward from the expired lock's expiration date, which is day zero. A relock request logged on the last day of the window is on time. The window length is the product's relock window. The check reads the lock's expiration date and the relock request's date in the lock request log for the same lock, before the relock is made.

**(b) Relocked rate and price.** This clause is no longer in force and has been superseded by the current basis for relock pricing. It was the former clause that the relocked rate and price are the worse for the borrower of the expired lock's terms and of the current rate-sheet terms on the relock pricing day. Under it, the locked rate stays the expired rate unless the market rate is higher, and the locked price becomes the higher of the expired locked price and the current rate-sheet price for that rate.

**(c) Relock fee.** This clause is no longer in force and has been superseded by the current basis for the relock fee. It was the former clause that the relock fee is the product's relock fee points, booked as a separate entry whose dollar cost equals the relock fee points times the loan amount at lock divided by 100, rounded to the cent.

**(d) New expiration date.** The new expiration date is the relock date plus the product's relock term in calendar days.

**(e) Number of relocks.** A lock may be relocked at most the product's maximum number of relocks. The count is the relock fee entries booked on the lock over its life up to today.

**(f) After the window.** After the window, or once the maximum number of relocks has been used, the lock is cancelled and the borrower takes a new lock at current market terms.

### Window boundary (hypothetical, with a 30-day window)

| Relock request logged | Counted from the expiration date (day zero) | On time |
|---|---|---|
| On the expiration date's following day | Day 1 | Yes |
| On the last day of the window | Day 30 | Yes |
| The day after | Day 31 | No: the lock is cancelled and a new lock at current market terms is needed |

*Hypothetical illustration:* a 30-day relock term starting on a relock date of the 3rd of a 31-day month gives a new expiration date on the 2nd of the following month.

superseded_clauses: The relocked rate and price are the worse for the borrower of the expired lock's terms and the current rate-sheet terms on the relock pricing day: the locked_rate stays the expired rate unless the market rate is higher, and lock_price_points becomes the higher of the expired lock_price_points and the current rate-sheet price for that rate.
The relock fee is relock_fee_points, booked as a separate entry with cost_amount equal to relock_fee_points times loan_amount_at_lock divided by 100, rounded to the cent.
